title: Decide private-docs signed-upload adoption or retirement
working_tree_status: dirty shared worktree; bounded USER-006 retained-route hardening and focused tests present
goal: Give the generic private-docs signed-upload route an explicit consumer contract or retire it with durable authorization and zero-caller evidence while preserving user privacy and storage boundaries

in: Exact caller inventory and an explicit adopt-versus-authorized-retire decision
Authentication, user-prefix normalization, expiry, rate-limit, cross-user denial, response, and storage-policy contract tests
out: Unrelated artist/music, venue, message-attachment, or workforce upload routes
Storage migrations, RLS policy mutation, hosted Supabase changes, bucket creation, or secret provisioning
USER-003 settings-family rewrite and USER-005 account-lifecycle implementation beyond their named private-docs dependencies
Endpoint deletion without an accepted retirement decision and refreshed zero-caller evidence

acceptance_criteria: A durable decision names either one canonical product consumer for this route or authorizes retirement after an exact zero-caller scan; absence alone is not retirement authorization

If adopted, the named consumer uses a documented path shape and the route proves authentication, normalized own-user prefix, bounded expiry, rate limiting, cross-user/path traversal denial, and fail-closed storage errors

If retired, route removal is accompanied by refreshed zero-caller and route-map evidence plus verification that settings certification upload, account deletion, and QA upload journeys use their approved paths
The private-docs storage-policy dependency is reviewed with the database owner; no application-layer prefix check is misrepresented as hosted RLS proof
Focused tests, lint, caller scan, route-map validation, diff validation, and control-plane validation pass
